about: READ-ONLY: renders what `commission-a-disk` WOULD do to a target, and writes nothing. It evaluates exactly the preconditions the write path evaluates — the target resolves under /dev/disk/by-id/, carries no partition table, and has nothing mounted on it and does not back / — and prints a plan document naming the resolved device, what was observed, the argv that would run and the effect. A target that fails any precondition gets the refusal instead, exit 78, because a plan for something that cannot run is not a plan. Declares NO approval: it mutates nothing, so it is the half of design 17835005 that can be used before the approval channel exists, and it is what a passkey will sign over once it does (q1: the signature binds a rendered plan, not a verb call — a verb call authorises an intent whose target can still resolve differently at execution time, which is exactly how the 2026-09-21 device renumbering would have gone wrong).
